newsitem.title: UK: LCE white sugar eases as buyers abandon market.
newsitem.headline: LCE white sugar eases as buyers abandon market.

text.p: London white sugar futures remained under pressure on Wednesday with no buyers in sight and business was confined to switches, traders said.
By 1541 GMT turnover was 1,077 lots, dominated by Oct/Dec spread deals at $4.50 and Oct/March at $10.50.
"We are not going to see any significant offtake unless the market comes down $10 basis October," said one trader.
"I don't think anyone can afford to buy this market unless he can sell physical sugar," he said.
Traders were awaiting the result of a Syrian tender to buy 26,000 tonnes of white sugar and 26,000 tonnes of raws for October shipment. No details were yet available.
The front-month October contract was trading at a session low of $349.00 a tonne, down $1.70 on the day.
The market shrugged off German statistician F.O. Licht's lower estimate on Wednesday for European beet sugar production.
"It can't have a bullish effect when there are no hold-ups in Brazil...there is India and there are no buyers," said the trader.
Licht's first estimate of European Union (EU) beet sugar output was 16.47 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97 compared with 16.997 million in 1995/96.
Total European beet output, including eastern and western European countries, was forecast at 27.827 million tonnes from 28.573 million in 1995/96.

Brokers Merrill Lynch said in their bi-weekly commodity report that although the market was pressurised by lack of demand, a possibility of lower crops in Cuba if financial aid is pulled out and likely Chinese purchases could limit the downside.
